content.text: No MFN or pricing-parity language exists anywhere in the agreement. I checked the fees section, maintenance charges, and general matters, and searched for parity terms ("favourable/favorable", "most favoured nation", "best", "other customers", "price", "discount", "third part") — nothing obliges Sparkling to extend Garman terms matching those given to third parties.

input.quote: Sparkling shall pay the fees as set out in the Fee Schedule in accordance with the terms of this Agreement and the Fee Schedule.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation or pricing-parity obligation of any kind. The fees clause (§ 11) simply requires payment per the Fee Schedule, the maintenance provisions (§ 10) contain only Garman-side service obligations, and General Matters (§ 20 / p0135-p0147) has no parity, price-matching or "no less favourable" covenant. Searches for "favourable/favorable", "most favoured nation", "best", "other customers", "price", "discount" and "third part" returned no parity language. Since nothing requires Sparkling to offer Garman terms matching those given to any third party, this sits at the playbook's preferred position (no MFN obligation on Customer), and no redline is warranted.
